reason: Conversation 1 matches the sensible first step: it explains 4C as a water supply fault and puts checking the under-sink valve first. It also says to unplug the machine before touching the hose, and it closes cleanly without unnecessary steps once the fault is fixed. Conversation 2 opens with a long, partly US-style generic reply (circuit breaker, 'usually the hot water line', removing the kick panel for the inlet filter, drain-loop checks) and lists inlet valve, flow meter and board faults. Its second turn is very good, though, linking the plumber's work to the valve and adding useful leak and drain blanking-cap checks. That helps it close the gap but does not outweigh the noisier, less accurate opening.
